user.title: Welcome to PLN Prepaid Monitor
user.description:
This integration watches your electricity usage, works out what it costs, estimates when your prepaid PLN token will run out, and warns you before it does.

**Important**: this integration only reads. It can never switch your electricity on or off, even though your smart breaker is capable of that.

The next step is adding your first energy source - for example your house or shop breaker.

data.add_source_now: Add the first energy source now

data_description.add_source_now: Untick this if you would rather set up sources later. You can add them at any time from the integration page.

pick_device.title: Pick the source device
pick_device.description: If you pick a device here, the fields on the next step will be filled in automatically from that device's sensors. You can still change everything. You may also leave this empty and pick each sensor yourself.

data_description.device_id: This list only contains devices that have an energy or power sensor, such as smart breakers, smart plugs, or inverters.
data_description.show_all_sensors: Tick this if the sensor you are looking for does not appear on the next step. That usually happens when the sensor does not tell Home Assistant what kind of measurement it reports.

map_entities.title: Map the sensors
map_entities.description:
Tell the system which sensor represents what. Only reading sensors are shown - buttons, relays, and device settings deliberately never appear here, so they cannot be picked by mistake.

Fill in at least one of Energy or Power.

data.name: Energy source name
data.unavailable_grace_minutes: Grace period before marking it offline (minutes)

data_description.name: The name you will see on the dashboard, for example 'House breaker' or 'Shop breaker'. Give it a clear name if you have more than one meter.
data_description.energy_entity_id: The kWh number that only ever goes up - like the odometer on a motorbike, it never decreases. In the Smart Life app this is usually called 'total forward energy'. This is the important one: when it is present, the system uses it as the primary basis for all calculations.
data_description.power_entity_id: The power being drawn right now, in Watts. It moves up and down constantly. Useful for a live load display. If the kWh sensor above is missing, the system will estimate kWh from this instead - that is an estimate and less accurate.
data_description.voltage_entity_id: The measured voltage, usually around 220 V. Display only; not used for cost calculations.
data_description.current_entity_id: The current flowing, in Amperes. Display only.
data_description.frequency_entity_id: Grid frequency, usually around 50 Hz. Not every meter has this - you may leave it empty.
data_description.availability_entity_id: If your device has a dedicated sensor telling you whether it is connected, pick it here. If left empty, the system works it out from the energy or power sensor above.
data_description.unavailable_grace_minutes: How long the source may disappear before it is marked genuinely offline. Short interruptions (WiFi or Zigbee dropping for a few seconds) are normal, so a small value such as 5 minutes is enough. During the grace period the last value is held, so it is not misread as 'no load'.
data_description.enabled: Untick to temporarily disable this source without deleting its settings.

abort.no_energy_sources: There are no energy sources yet. Add at least one energy source first, then create a billing group.

error.name_required: The billing group name cannot be empty.
error.name_duplicate: A billing group with that name already exists. Use a different name.
error.no_sources_selected: Pick at least one energy source for this group.
error.no_periods_selected: Pick at least one period. Without one, no usage counter is created.
error.thresholds_out_of_order: The thresholds must decrease in order: warning greater than critical, and critical greater than very critical.
error.preset_format_invalid: Some lines are not in the right format. Each line is either just the kWh figure (for example 826.50) or 'amount = kWh' (for example 1000000 = 826.50). A kWh figure above 20,000 is also refused - it is most likely the KWM unit from the receipt, which needs dividing by 100.

members.title: New billing group
members.description:
A billing group is one 'electricity bill' - one or more energy sources whose usage is counted together.

A common setup: one group called 'PLN House' holding the house breaker, and another called 'PLN Shop' holding the shop breaker. They are counted separately and each has its own token.

If one electricity bill of yours is measured by several meters at once, pick them all here - their usage is added up.

data_description.name: The name you will see on the dashboard, for example 'PLN House' or 'PLN Shop'.
data_description.source_ids: Tick every source that belongs to this electricity bill. If you only have one meter, tick just that one. If you tick a source already used by another group, you will get a warning on the last step.

cycles.title: Counting periods
cycles.description:
Choose which usage counters you want to see, and when each counter starts again from zero.

If you have no particular reason to change them, leave the defaults - they are sensible for most people.

data.month_start_day: Day of month a new month starts

data_description.cycle_periods: Each choice creates one sensor, for example 'usage today' or 'usage this month'. Untick the ones you do not need to keep your entity list tidy.
data_description.day_start_time: What time the daily counter starts again from zero. Usually midnight (00:00). Change it if you want 'a day' to start at another time, such as when your shop opens.
data_description.week_start_day: Which day the weekly counter starts again from zero.
data_description.month_start_day: Which day of the month the monthly counter starts again from zero. Use 1 to follow the normal calendar. Capped at 28 so the day always exists in every month, February included.
data_description.year_start_month: Which month the yearly counter starts again from zero. Use January to follow the normal calendar.

tariff.title: Electricity tariff
tariff.description: Pick the tariff this billing group uses. You may leave it empty - the group still counts kWh, it just will not calculate rupiah cost until a tariff is chosen.

data_description.tariff_id: If the tariff you need does not exist yet, close this form, add a tariff from the integration page, then start again.

token.title: PLN token tracking
token.description:
Turn this on if this billing group runs on **prepaid (token)** electricity and you want the system to track the remaining kWh.

The system cannot read your remaining token from PLN - there is no official service for that. What it does instead: each time you top up, you record how many kWh went in, and the system subtracts your real usage as measured by your meter.

The result is a token record that **stands on its own**, and does not break when your meter's built-in counter misbehaves.

data.token_enabled: Track remaining token for this group
data.reset_hold_threshold_kwh: Hold threshold when the meter resets (kWh)

data_description.token_enabled: Leave off if this group is on postpaid electricity, or if you only want usage monitoring without token tracking.
data_description.reset_hold_threshold_kwh: A safeguard for a rare event: if the meter resets and the first reading afterwards is larger than this, the system **freezes** the remaining-token figure and asks you first, instead of silently subtracting it from your balance. An ordinary firmware reset drops to nearly zero and will not trigger this. The default of 1 kWh is safe for most cases.
data_description.token_presets_text:
If you always buy the same number of kWh, put it here so you do not have to type it again every time. These values appear as one-click buttons on the dashboard.

One value per line. The easiest form is just the kWh figure:

`826.50`

To record the purchase amount as well, write **amount = kWh**:

`1,000,000 = 826.50`
`500,000 = 413.25`

The kWh figure comes from the receipt, under **Jumlah Kwh**. Careful: receipts often print it in units of 0.01 kWh - **82650 KWM** on the receipt means **826.50 kWh** on the meter display. Divide by 100 if the number looks far too large.

You can leave this empty. Once you record a top-up, that amount is remembered and its button appears on the dashboard on its own.

prediction.title: Warnings and estimates
prediction.description:
Set when the token counts as running low, and how the system estimates the days left.

Estimates come from your own average usage recorded in Home Assistant's history. **While there is not enough data, the system shows no figure at all** - better to admit it does not know than to give a date that sounds certain but was guessed from two days of usage.

If in doubt, leave everything as it is.

data.warning_threshold_days: Warn when fewer days remain than
data.critical_threshold_days: Critical when fewer days remain than
data.very_critical_threshold_days: Very critical when fewer days remain than
data.token_low_kwh_threshold: Very critical when remaining kWh drops below

data_description.warning_threshold_days: The first level. The default of 7 days gives you a week to buy a token without rushing.
data_description.critical_threshold_days: The second level; must be lower than the warning level.
data_description.very_critical_threshold_days: The final level; must be lower than critical. This is the level that will later be allowed through quiet hours.
data_description.token_low_kwh_threshold: An extra safeguard that does not depend on the estimate: whatever the day count says, remaining kWh below this counts as very critical straight away. Enter 0 to switch it off.
data_description.preferred_window: The time span used to work out your average daily usage. 7 days is the most balanced choice: long enough to smooth out unusual days, short enough to follow changing habits. If there is not enough data, the system falls back to another span and lowers its confidence.
data_description.min_data_points: How many days (or hours, for the 24-hour span) must be collected before the system will give a figure. Raising it makes estimates more cautious but slower to appear.
data_description.outlier_filter: How to damp days with unusual usage - guests staying over, air conditioning running all day - so one day does not skew the whole month ahead.
data_description.safety_margin_percent: Makes the estimate slightly pessimistic: it calculates as if your usage were this many percent higher. The point is to have you top up a little early rather than a little late.

notification.title: Token notifications
notification.description:
Choose where warnings go when the token runs low, and how often.

Messages are only sent **when the status changes level** - for example from normal to needs-attention. While the status stays the same, the system says nothing. A warning that arrives every five minutes simply stops being read.

If you already have the Telegram integration set up in Home Assistant, its targets appear automatically in the list below.

data.notify_on_recovery: Also tell me when the token is topped up again
data.bypass_quiet_hours_for_very_critical: Very critical may break through quiet hours

data_description.notify_enabled: Turn off if you only want to see the status on your dashboard without being messaged.
data_description.notify_targets: Pick one or more destinations. This list comes straight from your Home Assistant, so it only contains targets that actually work. You may leave it empty if a notification inside Home Assistant is enough.
data_description.create_persistent_notification: Shows the message in Home Assistant's notification bell. Useful as a fallback when Telegram is having trouble.
data_description.message_prefix: Put in front of every message. The default '[Token PLN]' makes it easy to tell apart from other automations you may already have, such as power-outage alerts.
data_description.notify_on_recovery: Sends one closing message when the status returns to normal, so you know it is sorted - rather than being left to guess.
data_description.repeat_while_unresolved: When on, the message repeats while the status stays at the same level. When off (the default), each level is announced once.
data_description.cooldown_hours: Only applies when repeating is on. Keeps the same message from arriving too close together.
data_description.quiet_hours_start: Start of the stretch you do not want to be disturbed, for example 22:00. Leave empty if not needed.
data_description.quiet_hours_end: End of that stretch, for example 06:00. Held messages are not lost - they go out once quiet hours are over.
data_description.bypass_quiet_hours_for_very_critical: Leave on if you still want to be woken when the power is genuinely about to go out.

error.name_required: The tariff name cannot be empty.
error.name_duplicate: A tariff with that name already exists. Use a different name.
error.rate_must_be_positive: The rate per kWh must be greater than zero.

tariff.title: Electricity tariff
tariff.description:
Enter your electricity tariff. One tariff can be shared by several billing groups - if your house and shop are on the same tariff category, one tariff covers both.

**The default of Rp {default_rate}/kWh is only an estimate** for category R-1 at 1300-2200 VA, gathered from tariff news reports, **not** an official PLN figure. You must adjust it to your own tariff category and region.

Where to find your real rate: your latest token purchase receipt, the PLN Mobile app, or an official PLN bill. Divide the rupiah amount that actually became kWh to estimate it.

Every time you change the rate here, the previous version is kept as history. Costs already recorded are not recalculated - which is correct, because that usage really did happen at the old rate.

data_description.name: A name to tell this tariff apart from others, for example 'R-1 900VA' or 'Shop tariff'.
data_description.rate_rp_per_kwh: The price of electricity per kWh for your PLN tariff category. The default is only an estimate - replace it with your actual rate.
data_description.fixed_charge_rp: A fixed charge billed even when you use no electricity. For prepaid residential PLN this is usually **0** - enter 0 if you are unsure. This field exists for business categories or unusual cases.
data_description.fixed_charge_period: Whether the standing charge above is billed daily or monthly. Has no effect when the standing charge is 0.
data_description.rounding_mode: How rupiah amounts are rounded for display. Rounding only affects what you see; the underlying calculation keeps full precision, so no error accumulates.
data_description.rounding_unit_rp: Round to multiples of how many rupiah. Enter 1 to round to the nearest rupiah, or 0 for no rounding at all.

topup_kwh.name: Top-up amount
topup_kwh.description: Enter how many kWh went in according to the receipt or the meter display, then press Record top-up. Nothing is recorded until you press the button.

meter_reading_kwh.name: Remaining token on the meter
meter_reading_kwh.description: Enter the remaining token shown on the physical meter, then press Match the meter reading. Use this when the system's figure has drifted from the meter.

warning_threshold_days.name: Warning threshold
warning_threshold_days.description: Token status becomes Warning below this many days remaining. Must be larger than the Critical threshold.

critical_threshold_days.name: Critical threshold
critical_threshold_days.description: Token status becomes Critical below this many days. Must sit between Warning and Very critical.

very_critical_threshold_days.name: Very critical threshold
very_critical_threshold_days.description: Token status becomes Very critical below this many days. Must be smaller than the Critical threshold.

rate_rp_per_kwh.name: Rate per kWh
rate_rp_per_kwh.description: Price of electricity per kWh. Changing it creates a new rate version - costs already recorded keep the rate that applied when that usage happened, so the past is never rewritten.

topup_rp.name: Purchase amount
topup_rp.description: How much you paid. You can fill in just this - the kWh figure is worked out from the tariff - or fill it in alongside the kWh box, which is the most accurate since both are printed on the receipt. Note: converting from the amount is only an estimate, because a real token purchase also carries admin fees, tax and stamp duty.

add_token_topup.name: Record token top-up
add_token_topup.description: Record electricity token you have just bought. The amount is added to what is left, not replacing it.

kwh_credited.name: kWh added
kwh_credited.description: How many kWh actually went into the meter, as shown on the receipt or the meter display. May be left empty if you fill in the purchase amount below and that amount has a ready-made value.

nominal_rp.name: Amount paid (Rp)
nominal_rp.description: How much you paid. If this amount is registered as a ready-made value, the kWh figure is taken from it automatically - you do not need to fill in kWh above.

timestamp.name: Top-up time
timestamp.description: Leave empty to use the current time. Fill it in if you are recording a token bought earlier.

meter_reading_before.name: Meter reading before top-up
meter_reading_before.description: Optional, for cross-checking. The remaining kWh shown on the meter before the token was entered.

meter_reading_after.name: Meter reading after top-up
meter_reading_after.description: Optional, for cross-checking. The remaining kWh shown on the meter after the token was entered.

note.name: Note
note.description: Free text, for example where you bought it or the token number.

calibrate_token_reading.name: Match the meter reading
calibrate_token_reading.description: Bring the system's figure in line with the remaining kWh shown on your physical meter. Use this when the two start to drift apart.

actual_remaining_kwh.name: Remaining kWh on the meter
actual_remaining_kwh.description: The number you can actually see on the meter right now. From that moment on, the system counts down from that figure.

note.name: Note
note.description: Why you calibrated, so the history makes sense later.

edit_topup.name: Correct a top-up record
edit_topup.description: Fix a mistyped top-up entry. The remaining token is recalculated from the whole history immediately.

topup_id.name: Entry ID
topup_id.description: The id of the entry to fix. You can find it in the history attribute on the remaining-token sensor.

kwh_credited.name: kWh added
kwh_credited.description: Fill in only if this is the value you want to change.

nominal_rp.name: Amount paid (Rp)
nominal_rp.description: Fill in only if this is the value you want to change.

timestamp.name: Top-up time
timestamp.description: Fill in only if the time is what you want to change.

delete_topup.name: Delete a top-up record
delete_topup.description: Remove a top-up entry that should not be there, for example one recorded twice.

topup_id.name: Entry ID
topup_id.description: The id of the entry to delete. You can find it in the history attribute on the remaining-token sensor.

reset_token_ledger.name: Start token tracking from zero
reset_token_ledger.description: Clear the remaining-token calculation and start again from zero. Use this when your physical meter has been replaced. The old history is kept as a record.

note.name: Note
note.description: Why you reset, for example 'meter replaced on 3 September'.

resolve_ledger_hold.name: Decide on a token hold
resolve_ledger_hold.description: Release the frozen remaining-token figure after the system detected a large meter reset.

action.name: Decision
action.description: Pick 'Treat as real usage' if that much electricity really was used; 'Ignore' if the meter was replaced or the number went wrong for reasons other than usage; 'Calibrate' if you want to enter the remaining figure shown on the meter.

generate_dashboard.name: Generate dashboard
generate_dashboard.description: Builds a Lovelace dashboard configuration for all your billing groups with the correct entity ids already filled in. Copy the WHOLE result and paste it into the Raw configuration editor of a new dashboard - this action does not change any existing dashboard.

layout.name: Layout
layout.description: Sections: cards can be dragged and dropped right on the dashboard, and are grouped per section. This is built into Home Assistant, not a third-party card. Masonry: the classic flowing layout, no drag and drop.

purge_old_data.name: Purge old data
purge_old_data.description: Deletes this integration's long-term history older than the retention limit. PERMANENT and cannot be undone. Your other entities and data are not touched.

keep_years.name: Keep history for
keep_years.description: One-off override of the retention setting. Leave empty to use the saved setting.

no_billing_group_selected.message: No billing group selected. Pick a billing group device as the target of this action.

token_not_enabled.message: Token tracking is not enabled for '{group}'. Turn it on via Reconfigure billing group, PLN token tracking step.

topup_not_found.message: There is no top-up entry with id '{topup_id}'. Check the history attribute on the remaining-token sensor.

ledger_not_on_hold.message: Token tracking for '{group}' is not on hold, so there is nothing to decide.

calibration_needs_reading.message: The 'Calibrate' option needs the remaining kWh shown on the meter.

no_billing_groups.message: There are no billing groups yet, so there is nothing to build a dashboard for.

topup_needs_kwh_or_nominal.message: Enter the kWh amount, or enter a purchase amount that has a ready-made value.

no_preset_for_nominal.message: There is no ready-made value for Rp {nominal}. Add one under Reconfigure billing group -> PLN token tracking, or enter the kWh amount yourself.

implausible_kwh.message: {kwh} kWh is too large for a single top-up. PLN receipts often write kWh in units of 0.01 - did you mean {hint} kWh?

retention_unlimited.message: Retention is still set to 'Forever', so nothing was deleted. Change it under Settings -> Devices & Services -> PLN Prepaid Monitor -> Configure, or fill in 'Keep history for' when calling this action.

retention_unsupported.message: Cleanup cannot run on this Home Assistant version: {reason}. Nothing was deleted. You can delete manually via Developer Tools -> Statistics.

amount_not_set.message: The amount is still empty. Fill in the number box above this button first, then press it.

thresholds_out_of_order.message: The thresholds are out of order. Warning must be larger than Critical, and Critical larger than Very critical.

no_rate_for_conversion.message: This group has no tariff, so a purchase amount cannot be converted into kWh. Fill in the kWh box instead, or link this group to a tariff first.

ledger_hold.title: Token tracking for {group} is on hold
ledger_hold.description:
Meter '{source}' jumped to {reset_to} kWh after its counter reset, so the remaining token for {group} has been frozen to avoid writing it off by mistake.

Please decide via the **Decide on a token hold** action:

- **Treat as real usage** - if that much electricity really was used.
- **Ignore** - if the meter was replaced, or the number went wrong for reasons other than usage.
- **Calibrate** - if you want to enter the remaining kWh shown on the meter.

init.title: Data maintenance
init.description:
Home Assistant's long-term history is **never purged automatically**. Over years of use, the database can keep growing.

Here you can limit how long this integration's history is kept.

⚠️ **Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.** Only history belonging to entities created by this integration is removed - your other entities and data are not touched at all.

data_description.statistics_retention_years: History older than this may be deleted. Pick 'Forever' if you do not want anything deleted - that is the default.
data_description.auto_purge_enabled: When on, cleanup runs by itself every day following the choice above. When off, cleanup only happens when you run the 'Purge old data' action yourself.
